clinician.final_diagnosis: Angiolymphoid Hyperplasia with Eosinophilia (ALHE) and scalp demodicosis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old female presented with 6-month history of pruritic, pearly papules and nodules on the left temporo-occipital scalp with secondary ulcerations and bleeding from scratching. Systemic examination was unremarkable without lymphadenopathy. Histopathological examination of skin biopsy revealed proliferation of blood vessels lined by plump histiocytoid endothelial cells with lymphocytic and eosinophilic dermal infiltrates, confirming ALHE, alongside Demodex mites in sebaceous ducts confirming demodicosis. Laboratory workup (CBC, renal function, IgE, HIV screening) was normal, notably without peripheral eosinophilia despite tissue eosinophilia. The patient was treated with 10 sessions of cryotherapy (2 freeze-thaw cycles per week) combined with twice-daily topical metronidazole gel, achieving remarkable clinical improvement within 7 weeks. She remained recurrence-free at 1-year follow-up.
